newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore gas oil swaps at 5-year high.
newsitem.headline: Singapore gas oil swaps at 5-year high.

text.p: Singapore gas oil (diesel) swaps rose to trade at a five-year high of $27.85 per barrel with the physical market poised to chalk a similar record on news of a U.S. air strike on Iraq, industry sources said on Tuesday.
Singapore gas oil swaps' previous record high of about $26.60 per barrel was recorded during the last winter, one refiner said.

The large increase to gas oil swaps were due to both the big jump in crude prices as well as the five-year high gas oil settlement on the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) on Monday, a trader said.
Crude prices have throughout the day been on the rise as news of the U.S. missile attack on air defence targets in Iraq filtered through.
SIMEX Brent crude opened trading at $22.90, up 91 cents from London's IPE close. It touched a high of $23.50 before easing to $22.35 on profit taking.
September gas oil on IPE closed on Monday at a 5-year high of $207.50 per tonne.
Traders said that the high IPE close left the Singapore market lagging and it was inevitable that prices rose to close the east-west price gap.
The big increase to swap prices is also expected to boost physical prices in Singapore, one refiner said. Latest gas oil swaps quotes were at $28.10-28.20, brokers said.
"As the east is still lagging the west in the recent price increases, there is no possibility of arbitrage cargoes heading this way from the west," the refiner added.
The absence of any product from the west is expected to allow producers in the east to easily place out its output, one trader said.
Refiners in Singapore were recently forced to cut crude runs as product prices were lower than their feedstock crude prices.
One refiner said that physical prices in Singapore should top the previous post-Gulf War record of $28.30 per barrel, seen in late February, within the next few days.
The market is firm despite a low diesel purchases by India as surplus product from Singapore and South Korea are finding a home in China and Indonesia.
